evidence: a-lan-and-a-wan-behind-the-node: cites the class purpose (pp:1-2, firewall config for an openvpn server); it is the setup for the forwarding checks, its namespaces sit on the fixture's interfaces (lan_bridge_iface p8test1, wan_iface p8test0), its declared mutates covers every action line (2 netns, 2 veth pairs, addresses/routes, 2 transient units, 2 appended p8test-default-drop rules), and the read-only effect (units active + 2 stand-in rules) shows the action's result, not its output

forward-bridge-loopback: pp:19 declares FORWARD iniface=outiface=$lan_bridge_iface, proto all, accept, no state; under the fixture that is -i p8test1 -o p8test1 without --state, -j ACCEPT, which is exactly the expect
nat-masquerade-on-wan: pp:21 declares nat POSTROUTING outiface $wan_iface, proto all, jump MASQUERADE; expect -o p8test0, no -p, -j MASQUERADE matches what the code produces under the fixture

purpose gap: Tested as behaviour: a LAN namespace behind p8test1 reaches a WAN server through the node and is seen as 10.252.0.1 (rules 202+205 forward and masquerade, counters confirm 202/203/205), a WAN host with a route into the LAN cannot open a connection (only 203 RELATED,ESTABLISHED passes, stand-in drop counted), ip_forward=1 live and persisted in /etc/sysctl.d; client_isolation is honestly uncovered (declared at pp:11, used nowhere, class warning pp:4-5). Gap: the hairpin outcome (pp:19, rule 204, traffic routed in and back out of the LAN bridge) is marked uncovered with lifted_by: ubuntu, which is this lab's default node itself; the stated reason is the set's own fixture choice (one veth with one client), not a lab limit: a Linux bridge p8test1 with two namespaces in two subnets routed via the node would send traffic in and out of p8test1, accepted only by rule 204 ahead of the stand-in -i p8test1 drop. The rule is only checked as installed (forward-bridge-loopback), so a part the lab can exercise is untested.
